title: Staggered acquisition playbook for intermittent surge capacity
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet sketches a staggered acquisition approach for handling short-duration surge demand (spikes from new customers, model launches, seasonal growth) without over-committing long-term capital. Target audience: infra procurement, SRE, product finance, and capacity planning leads.

High-level goal:
- Satisfy 8–12 week surge windows with a mix of short-term leases, staggered on-order shipments, and reserved buy-forward for core SKUs so hosted capacity stays within 95th percentile latency & availability targets.

Assumptions (rough):
- Baseline fleet: 6.5k effective GPU units across regions (US-E, US-W, EU, APAC).
- Typical lead times: OEM order -> 12–20 weeks (high variance), broker/lease -> 2–6 weeks, refurb -> 4–8 weeks.
- Surge profile: +20–40% peak over baseline, duration frequently 6–10 weeks.
- Budget window: allowed incremental opex for leasing up to 18% of baseline monthly spend during surge.

SKU mix candidate list (for planning):
- sku-A: nvx-90 (high perf FP16; latency-sensitive RT workloads)
- sku-B: nvx-80 (balanced perf/cost; batch generation)
- sku-C: t4-refurb (cost-tier for embeddings/low-priority)
- sku-D: burst-spot-large (elastic instances for best-effort throughput)

Lead-time waterfall (decision sketch):
1) Immediate (0–2w): shift routing to existing dedicated pools, enable tighter batching, turn on TTL-based cache borrowing between routes.
2) Short (2–6w): spin up broker leases; prioritize regionally local leases to reduce egress & latency impact.
3) Medium (6–12w): accept refurbished units and scheduled shipments (partial arrival windows).
4) Long (12–24w): new OEM orders to replenish baseline or transition to new SKU family.

Regional prioritization heuristics:
- US-E: prioritize low-latency sku-A for enterprise customers with SLA.
- US-W: flexible mix of sku-A/B; lean more on leased capacity for surges.
- EU: prefer sku-B and sku-C blended to reduce cost; use local brokers to avoid customs delays.
- APAC: prefer smaller, faster-arrival leases; avoid long OEM orders unless multi-quarter runway exists.

Staggering pattern (example for a 10-week surge requiring +30% capacity):
- Week 0–1: enable software mitigations, shift non-critical workload to preemptible pools.
- Week 1–3: lease 40% of additional needed capacity (broker) across impacted regions.
- Week 3–6: bring in 40% refurbished arrivals and begin partial routing.
- Week 6–10: schedule OEM phased deliveries for remaining 20% if forecasts still hold.

Mix hedging rules (quick heuristics):
- If forecasted surge probability > 60% and duration > 6 weeks -> prefer leases + 25% OEM forward buy.
- If surge is customer-specific (enterprise) -> secure lease with regional proximity + short OEM deposit.
- If surge is speculative (marketing-driven) -> lean on preemptible burst lanes and spot reservations.

Operational playbook checkpoints (action checklist):
- [ ] Forecast confirmation: Product/Customer success sign-off on demand window (owner: Prod Ops).
- [ ] Budget approval: Finance ok for incremental opex/one-time capex (owner: Finance BP).
- [ ] Broker quotes: collect 3 bids per region for lease/refurb options (owner: Procurement).
- [ ] Shipping windows: align logistics for 2–4 partial arrivals (owner: Ops).
- [ ] SRE routing: define canary traffic split and fallback policies (owner: SRE).
- [ ] Billing mapping: map leased units to cost center tags for show-back (owner: FinOps).

Vendor and procurement notes (informal):
- Preferred brokers: NorthHarbor Leasing (US), EuroCompute Exchange (EU), PacificLease (APAC).
- Ask vendors for firm lead-time windows and contingency commitments (partial refunds / credit if >14d slip).
- For refurb, require burn-in & KV cache validation on arrival; assign 48h soak time before production routing.

Quick cost model snapshot (text table):
- Baseline monthly GPU opex: $1.2M
- 30% surge leasing for 6 weeks (estimated): +$160k incremental opex over window
- Refurb arrivals: one-time onboarding ops FY cost: ~$22k per 100 units
- OEM forward deposit: ~20% of order value if used

Risk register (short bullets):
- Customs / import delay (EU/APAC): mitigation -> prefer broker-sourced local inventory.
- Quality issues on refurb: mitigation -> require burn-in + SLA with return window.
- Forecast miss (overbuy): mitigation -> include resale/return clause or convert to Dedicated pool credits.
- Price swings: mitigation -> staggered OEM tranches, negotiate FX pass-throughs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need precise region-by-region burn rates per workload class (SRE to provide per-route token burn estimates) [owner: Riley Park].
- Confirm maximum short-term lease ceiling from legal (term & indemnity constraints).
- Evaluate feasibility of consignment inventory with a broker (vendor stores inventory in-region, we pay on-draw).

References / links:
- Related runbook: procurement-priority-trigger-scorecard (see drive; ticket JIRA-3318).
- Slack thread: #procurement-ops, message ts 1700520000 (Nov 20 proto discussion).
- Infra repo PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 (lease automation updates).

Notes to self (rough):
- This doc = quick operational checklist + decision heuristics, not the final SOW.
- Want to push a small automation: when forecasted surge > X, auto-open vendor RFQ template and tag finance reviewer.

Decision log (snapshot):
- 2024-11-15: agreed to test a two-broker pilot for US-W leases. (owners: Procurement + Ops)
- 2024-11-22: SRE validated 10% additional route-level batch gain possible — update surge sizing accordingly.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Procurement: collect broker quotes and term sheets (due 2024-11-20) -> assigned to Amit Patel.
- SRE: produce per-route burn chart & recommended fallback splits (due 2024-11-25) -> assigned to Riley Park.
- Finance: draft surge budget addendum for 6–12 week windows (due 2024-11-26) -> assigned to Sofia Alvarez.

End of sheet.

(Informal notes: feel free to scribble over this — it's intentionally fuzzy for quick iteration.)
